company: Janssen Biotech, Inc. (letter addressed to Johnson & Johnson International, Inc.)
regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (responder subset / maintenance trial)
cases.claim: “Many people experienced remission at 1 and even 2 years” (AVO) | “~1 out of 2 patients were in clinical remission at 1 year and at 2 years” (SUPER) | “MANY PEOPLE EXPERIENCED REMISSION at 1 and even 2 years” (SUPER)
cases.context: UC2 maintenance enrolled only Week-12 responders (38-39% non-responders excluded); 2-year data from LTE subset of a subset.
cases.rationale: Applying maintenance/LTE responder rates to all treated patients overstates remission and durability.
cases.check: Are rates from randomized-withdrawal/maintenance or extension responder subsets presented as if they apply to all treated patients?

cases.claim: “Some saw one hundred percent visible healing of their intestinal lining” (AVO, 0:18) | “Some saw 100% VISIBLE HEALING of their intestinal lining” (SUPER) | “Healing is possible with Tremfya” (AVO, 0:34) | “HEALING IS POSSIBLE with Tremfya® (guselkumab)” (SUPER)
cases.context: Disclaimer 'Visually assessed areas may not represent remission of the entire colon lining. Individual results may vary.' does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Implies curative 'healing'; endoscopic endpoints don't guarantee long-term outcomes.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'heal/healing/cure/100%' language in chronic-disease efficacy claims.

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (responder subset / maintenance trial)
cases.claim: “1 out of 3 patients achieved endoscopic remission at one year” (SUPER, 0:18 and 0:34)
cases.context: 35%/34% at Week 44 in UC2 responder population.
cases.rationale: Suggests a third of all treated patients achieve endoscopic remission.
cases.check: Is the denominator for a quoted rate (e.g., responders only) disclosed and consistent with the implied population?

cases.claim: The major statement does not communicate: “TREMFYA is a medicine that may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections.”
cases.rationale: Omits material infection risk from major statement.
cases.check: Rule: Medication Guide 'most important information' items must appear in a TV ad's major statement.
